title: Prepositions of Movement: across, along, through, over, past
grammarTitle: Prepositions of Movement — describing how you get there
grammarNote: Предлоги движения описывают, КАК вы перемещаетесь. Они связаны с маршрутом, а не с местом. В английском каждый предлог передаёт конкретный тип движения: across = с одной стороны на другую; along = вдоль; through = насквозь; over = сверху/через; under = под; past = мимо; into/out of = в/из; round = вокруг.

grammarTable.subject: across

grammarTable.example: "Walk ACROSS the road." / "Swim ACROSS the river." / "Go ACROSS the park."

grammarExtra.title: across vs through — an important distinction

rows.form: across = from one side to the other (open space)
rows.example: "Walk ACROSS the road." / "ACROSS the bridge." / "ACROSS the square."

rows.form: through = enter and exit an enclosed space
rows.example: "Walk THROUGH the tunnel." / "THROUGH the park (enclosed by fences)." / "THROUGH the forest."

rows.form: Test: is it open or enclosed?
rows.example: Open (road, field, river) → ACROSS. Enclosed (tunnel, forest, building) → THROUGH.

rows.form: Some overlap: "through the park" OK too
rows.example: Parks can use either. "Walk across the park" (open feel) / "through the park" (it has gates/paths). Both ✅

grammarExtra.title: over vs under — above or below

rows.example: "Walk OVER the bridge." (you walk on top of it) / "Jump OVER the wall."
"Walk UNDER the bridge." (you pass beneath it) / "Go UNDER the railway."

rows.form: Both refer to the same structure from different positions
rows.example: "We walked OVER the bridge." vs "There's a tunnel that goes UNDER the road."
"We walked THROUGH the tunnel." (entered, walked inside, exited) — not over or under.

grammarExtra.title: along vs past — direction or point of reference

rows.example: "Walk ALONG the river." / "Drive ALONG Dostyq Avenue." = the whole length.

rows.form: past = go beyond a specific point
rows.example: "Walk PAST the mosque." / "Drive PAST the bank." = at that point and continue.
"Walk ALONG the main road until you go PAST the mosque."
"Walk INTO the building." (entering) ↔ "Come OUT OF the building." (exiting)

rows.form: round = in a circle / around something
rows.example: "Go ROUND the roundabout." / "Walk ROUND the lake." / "Turn ROUND the corner."
"Go UP the stairs." / "Walk DOWN the hill." / "Climb UP the steps."
"Walk TO the library." / "Go TO the bus stop." (destination, not route)
"Walk TOWARDS the mosque." (heading that way, may not arrive)

grammarTip:
Предлоги движения — ключевые различия:
① ACROSS = с одной стороны на другую (открытое пространство):
→ "cross the road" / "across the bridge"
② THROUGH = войти и выйти из закрытого пространства:
→ "through the tunnel" / "through the park"
③ ALONG = вдоль чего-то (по всей длине):
→ "along the river" / "along the avenue"
④ PAST = мимо (не останавливаясь):
→ "past the bank" / "past the mosque"
⑤ OVER = над / сверху. UNDER = под.
→ "over the bridge" (шли по нему) vs "under the bridge" (прошли под ним)

💡 into = вход. out of = выход:
"walk INTO the building" / "come OUT OF the tunnel"

exercises.text: Walk ___ the road at the pedestrian crossing — it's safer.
exercises.hint: "across" = from one side to the other (open space like a road). "Walk ACROSS the road." ✅

exercises.text: Walk ___ the tunnel — it's only thirty seconds.
exercises.hint: "through" = enter and exit an enclosed space. "Walk THROUGH the tunnel." ✅

exercises.text: Go ___ the mosque without stopping — the bank is further on.
exercises.hint: "past" = go beyond a point without stopping. "Go PAST the mosque." ✅

exercises.text: We walked ___ the bridge to reach the eastern bank of the river.
exercises.hint: "over the bridge" = walked on top of / across it. "We walked OVER the bridge." ✅

exercises.text: Walk ___ the river path until you reach the park.
exercises.hint: "along" = following the length of something. "Walk ALONG the river path." ✅

exercises.instruction: Complete with into or out of.
exercises.text: She walked ___ the building quickly. Five minutes later, she came ___ with a book.
exercises.hint: "into" = entering. "out of" = exiting. "walked INTO the building / came OUT OF." ✅

exercises.text: He walked ___ the park (which has fences and paths and feels enclosed).
exercises.hint: "through" = enclosed space with entry and exit. Fenced park = "through the park." ✅

exercises.text: Go ___ the roundabout and take the second exit.
exercises.hint: "round the roundabout" = in a circular direction. "Go ROUND the roundabout." ✅

exercises.text: Walk ___ the avenue, ___ the bank, then ___ the street to reach the library.
exercises.hint: along (following length) + past (go beyond bank) + across (cross the street).

exercises.text: There's a path ___ the railway that goes through a tunnel.
exercises.hint: "under the railway" = a path going below the railway line. "UNDER the railway." ✅

exercises.text: Go ___ the hill and you'll see the village on the other side.
exercises.hint: "over the hill" = go above and across. "Go OVER the hill." ✅

opts: "Walk along the road at the pedestrian crossing."
"Walk across the road at the pedestrian crossing."
"Walk through the road at the pedestrian crossing."
"Walk past the road at the pedestrian crossing."
exercises.correct: "Walk across the road at the pedestrian crossing."
exercises.hint: "across" = from one side to the other of an open space (a road). ✅

questions.text: "Walk ___ the road." (from one side to the other)
questions.hint: "across" = open space, one side to the other. "Walk ACROSS the road." ✅
"through" = enclosed space, enter and exit. "Walk THROUGH the tunnel." ✅
"along" = following the length of. "Walk ALONG the river bank." ✅
"past" = go beyond a specific point without stopping. "Go PAST the bank." ✅

questions.text: "We walked ___ the bridge." (we walked on top of it)
questions.hint: "over the bridge" = you walked on top of / across it. "We walked OVER the bridge." ✅
"under the railway" = the path goes below it. "A path UNDER the railway." ✅

questions.text: "Go ___ the roundabout and take the first exit."
questions.hint: "round the roundabout" = circling it. "Go ROUND the roundabout." ✅

questions.text: "Come ___ the tunnel — you can see it now." (exiting)
questions.hint: "out of" = exiting. "Come OUT OF the tunnel." ✅

questions.text: What is the difference between "across" and "through"?
questions.hint: "across" = open area (road, field). "through" = enclosed space (tunnel, forest, building).

questions.text: "Walk ___ the park." (the park has fences and paths — enclosed)
questions.hint: Enclosed park with fences → "through". "Walk THROUGH the park." ✅

questions.text: "She went ___ the corner." (she went around the bend)
questions.hint: "round the corner" = went around the bend. "She went ROUND the corner." ✅

questions.text: "Go ___ the hill and turn right." (climb and cross over)
questions.hint: "over the hill" = go above and across to the other side. ✅

questions.text: "Walk ___ the avenue as far as the mosque."
questions.hint: "along" = following the length. "Walk ALONG the avenue." ✅

questions.text: "He ran ___ the building to get inside."
questions.hint: "into" = entering. "He ran INTO the building to get inside." ✅

questions.text: "Towards" is different from movement prepositions because:
opts: It shows direction only, not arrival
questions.correct: It shows direction only, not arrival
questions.hint: "towards" = heading in the direction of — you may not arrive. "to" = you reach the destination.
